variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A Transformer is a neural-network architecture that moves information between sequence positions with attention. Each position creates a query, compares it with keys from positions it is allowed to read, and blends their values into a new contextual representation.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Choose the architecture around the information boundary”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Encoder-only
pairs.detail: Every non-padding token can usually attend across the full input.
pairs.explanation: Every non-padding token can usually attend across the full input. This fits representation tasks such as classification, extraction, ranking, and embedding. BERT is the canonical example.

pairs.label: Decoder-only
pairs.detail: Each position can attend only to itself and earlier positions.
pairs.explanation: Each position can attend only to itself and earlier positions. The model predicts the next token repeatedly, which fits open-ended generation and tool-using language models.

pairs.label: Encoder-decoder
pairs.detail: The encoder builds source representations; the decoder uses causal self-attention plus cross-attention to that source.
pairs.explanation: The encoder builds source representations; the decoder uses causal self-attention plus cross-attention to that source. This fits transformations such as translation and structured rewriting. T5 uses this family.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is attention may combine only information allowed by the model's task contract.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Encoder-only: Every non-padding token can usually attend across the full input. Decoder-only: Each position can attend only to itself and earlier positions. Encoder-decoder: The encoder builds source representations; the decoder uses causal self-attention plus cross-attention to that source.

pairs.label: Mask leakage
pairs.detail: Future labels or tokens become visible during training, so evaluation looks strong while causal generation fails in production.
